The **Women's Team Archery event** at the **2012 Summer Olympics** in **London** was one of the most exciting competitions in the sport, featuring top archers from around the world. Here’s a detailed breakdown of everything you need to know:

---

### **1. Event Overview**
- **Discipline:** Recurve (Olympic-style archery)
- **Format:** Team event (3 archers per country)
- **Dates:** **July 27–29, 2012** (qualification on July 27, elimination rounds on July 29)
- **Venue:** **Lord’s Cricket Ground** (a historic and iconic location, making it one of the most unique Olympic archery venues)
- **Number of Teams:** **12 teams** (36 archers total)
- **Scoring System:**
  - **Qualification Round (July 27):** Each archer shot **72 arrows** (12 ends of 6 arrows) at a distance of **70 meters**. The top 4 teams advanced directly to the quarterfinals, while teams ranked 5–12 played in the **1/8 elimination round**.
  - **Elimination Rounds (July 29):** Teams shot **24 arrows (8 ends of 3 arrows per archer)** in a **set system** (best of 5 sets, with 6 arrows per set). The team with the highest score in each set won 2 points; a tie gave 1 point. First to **5 points** advanced.

---

### **2. Participating Teams (12 Nations)**
| **Rank** | **Team** | **Archers** | **Qualification Score** |
|----------|----------|-------------|-------------------------|
| 1        | **South Korea** | Ki Bo-bae, Choi Hyeonju, Lee Sung-jin | **1,993** (Olympic Record) |
| 2        | **China** | Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing | **1,946** |
| 3        | **Japan** | Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie, Kaori Kawanaka | **1,938** |
| 4        | **Russia** | Ksenia Perova, Kristina Timofeeva, Inna Stepanova | **1,936** |
| 5        | **Denmark** | Carina Christiansen, Maja Jager, Louise Laursen | **1,886** |
| 6        | **Mexico** | Mariana Avitia, Aída Román, Alejandra Valencia | **1,883** |
| 7        | **Chinese Taipei** | Le Chien-ying, Lin Chia-en, Tan Ya-ting | **1,871** |
| 8        | **India** | Deepika Kumari, Bombayla Devi Laishram, Chekrovolu Swuro | **1,867** |
| 9        | **Italy** | Pia Lionetti, Jessica Tomasi, Natalia Valeeva | **1,843** |
| 10       | **Great Britain** | Naomi Folkard, Amy Oliver, Alison Williamson | **1,843** |
| 11       | **Ukraine** | Tetyana Dorokhova, Kateryna Palekha, Lidiia Sichenikova | **1,837** |
| 12       | **USA** | Miranda Leek, Khatuna Lorig, Jennifer Nichols | **1,837** |

**Key Notes:**
- **South Korea** dominated the qualification round, setting an **Olympic Record (1,993)**.
- **Great Britain** (host nation) and **Italy** had identical scores (1,843), with GB ranked higher due to a better **X-count** (arrows hitting the innermost ring).
- **India’s Deepika Kumari** was a strong medal contender but struggled in the team event.

---

### **3. Elimination Rounds & Results**
#### **1/8 Elimination Round (July 29)**
- **Denmark** def. **Ukraine** (211–206)
- **Mexico** def. **USA** (219–215)
- **Chinese Taipei** def. **Italy** (217–216)
- **India** def. **Great Britain** (218–210)

#### **Quarterfinals**
- **South Korea** def. **India** (220–207)
- **China** def. **Chinese Taipei** (210–209)
- **Japan** def. **Mexico** (219–209)
- **Russia** def. **Denmark** (216–206)

#### **Semifinals**
- **South Korea** def. **Japan** (221–206)
- **China** def. **Russia** (208–207)

#### **Bronze Medal Match**
- **Japan** def. **Russia** (209–207)

#### **Gold Medal Match**
- **South Korea** def. **China** (210–209)

**Final Standings:**
🥇 **South Korea** (Ki Bo-bae, Choi Hyeonju, Lee Sung-jin)
🥈 **China** (Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing)
🥉 **Japan** (Ren Hayakawa, Miki Kanie, Kaori Kawanaka)

---

### **4. Key Highlights & Memorable Moments**
✅ **South Korea’s Dominance:**
- South Korea won its **7th consecutive Olympic gold** in the women’s team event (since 1988).
- **Ki Bo-bae** (who also won individual gold) was the star, hitting multiple **10s and Xs** under pressure.
- Their **team score of 221 in the semifinal** was an Olympic record at the time.

✅ **China’s Near-Upset:**
- China pushed South Korea to the limit in the final, losing by just **1 point (209–210)**.
- **Xu Jing** shot a **perfect 30 in the 4th set**, but South Korea’s consistency prevailed.

✅ **Japan’s Historic Bronze:**
- Japan won its **first-ever Olympic archery medal** (team or individual) in **44 years** (since 1968).
- **Ren Hayakawa** (who later won individual bronze in 2016) was a key performer.

✅ **India’s Disappointment:**
- **Deepika Kumari** (world #1 at the time) and her team were eliminated in the **quarterfinals** by South Korea.
- India’s performance was marred by **windy conditions** at Lord’s, which affected their accuracy.

✅ **Lord’s Cricket Ground as a Venue:**
- Archery was held at **Lord’s**, the "Home of Cricket," in front of a **sold-out crowd**.
- The **temporary archery range** was set up on the **outfield**, with the famous **Pavilion** in the background.
- The **rain delay** on July 29 added drama to the elimination rounds.

---

### **5. Individual Performances & Statistics**
- **Top Scorers in Qualification (Team Event):**
  1. **Ki Bo-bae (KOR)** – 671 (individual 1st)
  2. **Choi Hyeonju (KOR)** – 669
  3. **Lee Sung-jin (KOR)** – 653
  4. **Cheng Ming (CHN)** – 664
  5. **Fang Yuting (CHN)** – 657

- **Highest Team Set Score in Elimination Rounds:**
  - **South Korea (221 vs. Japan, Semifinal)**

- **Closest Match:**
  - **China vs. Russia (Semifinal)** – China won **208–207** (decided by a single arrow).

---

### **6. Aftermath & Legacy**
- **South Korea’s Dynasty Continues:**
  - This was their **7th straight gold** in the women’s team event (1988–2012).
  - They would go on to win again in **2016 (Rio)** and **2020 (Tokyo)**.

- **Japan’s Rise:**
  - The bronze medal marked the beginning of Japan’s **archery resurgence**, culminating in **gold in Tokyo 2020**.

- **China’s Consistency:**
  - China remained a **top contender**, winning silver in **2016** and **2020**.

- **Deepika Kumari’s Redemption:**
  - After a disappointing 2012, she won **gold at the 2018 Asian Games** and **World Championships (2021)**.

- **Lord’s Cricket Ground’s Unique Legacy:**
  - The venue was praised for its **atmosphere**, though some archers struggled with **wind and rain**.
  - It remains one of the most **iconic Olympic archery venues** in history.

---

### **7. Fun Facts**
- **Oldest Archer:** **Natalia Valeeva (Italy, 42 years old)** – A veteran competing in her **5th Olympics**.
- **Youngest Archer:** **Ren Hayakawa (Japan, 21 years old)** – Went on to win **individual bronze in 2016**.
- **First-Time Olympians:** **12 of the 36 archers** were competing in their first Olympics.
- **Most Experienced Team:** **South Korea** (all three archers had **Olympic experience**).
- **Home Disadvantage?** **Great Britain** (hosts) were eliminated in the **1/8 round** by India.

---

### **8. Where Are They Now? (2024 Update)**
| **Archer** | **Country** | **Post-2012 Career** |
|------------|------------|----------------------|
| **Ki Bo-bae** | South Korea | Won **individual gold (2012, 2016)**, retired in 2017, now a **coach**. |
| **Choi Hyeonju** | South Korea | Competed in **2016**, now a **national team coach**. |
| **Lee Sung-jin** | South Korea | Retired after **2016**, works in **sports administration**. |
| **Cheng Ming** | China | Competed in **2016**, now a **commentator**. |
| **Ren Hayakawa** | Japan | Won **individual bronze (2016)**, retired in 2021. |
| **Deepika Kumari** | India | **World #1 (2021)**, won **gold at 2021 World Championships**, still active. |
| **Khatuna Lorig** | USA | Competed in **5 Olympics (1992–2016)**, now a **coach**. |

---

### **9. Full Medal Match Breakdown (South Korea vs. China)**
| **Set** | **South Korea** | **China** | **Set Winner** |
|---------|----------------|-----------|----------------|
| 1       | 56             | 55        | **South Korea (2–0)** |
| 2       | 55             | 55        | **Tie (2–1)** |
| 3       | 56             | 55        | **South Korea (4–1)** |
| 4       | 53             | 54        | **China (4–3)** |
| 5       | 50             | 50        | **Tie (5–5)** → **Shoot-off** |

**Shoot-off (1 arrow per archer):**
- **South Korea:** 27 (Ki Bo-bae 9, Choi Hyeonju 9, Lee Sung-jin 9)
- **China:** 26 (Cheng Ming 9, Fang Yuting 8, Xu Jing 9)
- **Result:** **South Korea wins 210–209**

---

### **10. Conclusion**
The **2012 Women’s Team Archery event** was a **thrilling competition** that showcased **South Korea’s dominance**, **China’s resilience**, and **Japan’s breakthrough**. The **unique venue at Lord’s Cricket Ground** added to the spectacle, making it one of the most **memorable Olympic archery events** in history.
